body:
The Vector is supposed to get filled, so it should use `r_` prefix.
```suggestion
	void get_arc_points(Vector<Point2> &r_points, const Vector2 &p_center, real_t p_major, real_t p_minor, real_t p_start_angle, real_t p_end_angle, int p_point_count);
```
This is a corner case, but after reparenting the CanvasItem to another viewport, the debug item will use wrong canvas. Maybe the debug canvas item should be freed instead of hidden when exiting tree?
Why this isn't under `show_rect` check? It's not needed if it won't draw anything.
Also redundant. You can move TOOLS_ENABLED one line higher.
Also pointless. No need for canvas item if it's not going to draw.

This one and the one above are required since preparation also includes clearing the canvas so it's ready for drawing (or making a blank one if it doesn't exist).

If these conditions end up changed so it wouldn't show anymore, it wouldn't clear it and it would stay visible.

Maybe I should name it prepare_and_clear_debug_canvas_item() to make it more apparent?
Is there a way to test this corner case? The hide/show thing seems to be for the purpose of faster undo, from what I have seen. I used to queue free stuff before but it has not been... ideal.

Makes sense then.
You could call `_prepare_debug_canvas_item()` only when the item was already created, but it's fine either way.

Try this scene:
[ViewportTest.tscn.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22882842/ViewportTest.tscn.txt)
Run with visible collision shapes and press the button to reparent shape to another viewport. The shape should disappear (it doesn't).
You don't need to make `rs` variable everywhere 🤔
I wonder how useful are these null checks. They aren't even consistent, some methods don't do that.
It would be fine to have single method that updates both modulate and self_modulate.
I would usually do it when there is more than one call to it, but I guess these don't have it, at least at the moment xD

I am noticing general inconsistencies, now that you mention it. My thought was that if the debug_canvas_item is valid, rs would have to exist at this point, which would only be false if rs got freed while the canvas items exist (which I find unlikely).

I will try and standardize this.

```suggestion
	void get_arc_points(LocalVector<Point2> &r_points, const Vector2 &p_center, real_t p_major, real_t p_minor, real_t p_start_angle, real_t p_end_angle, int p_point_count);
```
If COW functionality isn't needed

```suggestion
				rs->canvas_item_add_primitive(_get_debug_canvas_item(), pts, cols, Vector<Vector2>(), RID()); // Small arrow.
```

Copy-On-Write, `Vector` is shared so when you pass it it doesn't copy all the data, but whenever you modify it it gets copied if it has any other copies, this adds some overhead when you operate on it which can be an issue, see [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/architecture/core_types.html#allocating-memory) for some details
I tried to replace it now, but the next call for canvas_item_add_polyline expects a proper vector, so I dunno if it's worth changing all of it.
That sounds like a good reason to keep it the way it is, thank you for checking!
